No—under those conditions, you should not be able to see the Moon.

Its altitude is **−6.883°**, meaning it is nearly 7° below the true horizon. Even though it is **81.9% illuminated** and the sky is clear, an ordinary observer cannot see it below a level, unobstructed horizon. Atmospheric refraction near the horizon lifts objects by only about 0.5–0.6°, far short of what is needed.

The Moon’s azimuth, **10.2°** (roughly north-northeast), tells you where it would rise, but at 10:31 UTC it is still below the horizon there. You might see it once it rises—roughly later in the day, depending on the exact horizon and terrain—but not at the stated time from Reykjavik.
